headline: No run today — Un1t class plus a 2h outdoor ride, but sleep debt is the thing to manage.
body_state: Deterministic verdict is **red**, driven by sleep: 27h of 14-day sleep debt, only 5.9h last night (sleep score 61). Garmin's own readiness score reads 77, but the internal composite (which folds in that debt) sits at 61.3 — moderate, not great. Body battery recharged well overnight (+45) and skin temp is normal (-0.8°C, no illness signal), HRV is balanced/above-normal. Load-wise you're in the productive zone (TSB -7, the -5…-30 sweet spot) even though Garmin's training-status label still reads "Unproductive." Net: body is coping with load fine, sleep is the deficit to fix.
training: Two booked sessions today, no run: **Un1t class** (45min Cardio) and a **2h outdoor ride**. Nothing from the running plan lands today — the next run is tomorrow's 9km Easy + Strides. Yesterday's 10x200m Speed Reps already put real intensity in the legs (RPE 8, HR into Z4/Z5 for 9+ min), so today's two sessions should stay aerobic: keep the ride at genuine Z2 recovery effort and don't chase the Z5/Z6 peaks in Un1t the way Aug 15's class did on a similarly red-flagged morning. On 5.9h of sleep, that restraint matters more than usual.
recent: Aug 17 speed reps: 8 of 10 200m reps ran 2-8% slower than target pace, cooldown cut to under 5 of the prescribed 10min — the stimulus landed, but execution has room. Aug 15 Un1t class pushed into Z5/Z6 (23min at 70-80%+ HR) on a red-readiness morning, working against that day's gate. The grey-zone pattern flagged all block continues: 21.6% easy / 51.7% moderate running time against an 80% easy target — Un1t + rides are filling days that should be recovery, which is exactly why easy runs keep coming in short and hard.
focus: Sleep debt (27h over 14 days) — earlier bedtime for the next two weeks, not just tonight.
Keep today's Un1t + ride genuinely aerobic — one hard stimulus (yesterday's speed work) per 48h is enough.
Tomorrow's easy run: hold 4:51-5:20/km to start pulling the easy/moderate ratio back toward 80%.
